name: Tokyo
intro: A giant, safe and spotless city of neighbourhoods: old temples in Asakusa, neon in Shinjuku and Shibuya, gardens, science museums and great food everywhere. Trains link it all.

transit.card: Suica or PASMO IC card (also in phone wallets)
transit.note: Trains run from about 5:00 to just after midnight; avoid rush hour 7:30–9:30.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Asakusa & Skytree
areas.blurb: Old Tokyo's temple district and the tallest tower.

areas.name: Ueno Park
areas.blurb: Museums, a zoo and a lively market street.

areas.name: Imperial Palace, Ginza & Tsukiji
areas.blurb: Palace gardens, smart shopping and the fish market streets.

areas.name: Shibuya & Harajuku
areas.blurb: The famous crossing, Meiji Shrine and youth street fashion.

areas.name: Shinjuku
areas.blurb: Skyscrapers, a free observatory and a big garden.

areas.name: Tokyo Tower
areas.blurb: The red tower and the temple at its foot.

areas.name: Toyosu & Odaiba
areas.blurb: Digital art museum, science museum and the bay.

areas.name: Mitaka (Ghibli Museum)
areas.blurb: The animation museum in a park in western Tokyo.

pois.name: Senso-ji Temple
pois.why: Tokyo's oldest temple, entered through the huge red lantern of the Thunder Gate.
pois.kid: Shake an omikuji fortune stick: if it's bad luck, tie the paper to the rack.

pois.name: Nakamise shopping street
pois.why: The 250 m lane of snack and souvenir stalls leading to Senso-ji.
pois.kid: Try a warm ningyo-yaki cake shaped like a lantern or a pigeon.
pois.tip: Locals don't eat while walking: stand by the stall to finish.

pois.name: Tokyo Skytree
pois.why: The 634 m broadcasting tower with decks at 350 m and 450 m.
pois.kid: Stand on the glass floor panels on the 340 m floor.
pois.tip: Sunset slots are popular: buy a timed ticket online.

pois.name: Sumida River water bus
pois.why: Boats from Asakusa down the river towards Hama-rikyu and Odaiba.

pois.name: Ueno Park
pois.why: A big park of temples, a lotus pond and museums.
pois.tip: Cherry blossom here is famous in late March and early April.

pois.name: Tokyo National Museum
pois.why: Japan's oldest museum: samurai armour, swords, kimono and Buddhist art.
pois.kid: Find the samurai armour with the scariest face mask.

pois.name: National Museum of Nature and Science
pois.why: Dinosaurs, a whale outside and hands-on science galleries.
pois.kid: The life-size blue whale stands outside the entrance.

pois.name: Ueno Zoo
pois.why: Japan's oldest zoo, opened in 1882, right inside Ueno Park.

pois.name: Ameya-Yokocho market street
pois.why: A busy market street under the train tracks: fruit on sticks, snacks and street food.

pois.name: Akihabara Electric Town
pois.why: Floors and floors of games, anime, models and retro consoles.
pois.kid: Try the arcade claw machines (and set a budget first).
pois.tip: Some upper floors of shops are for adults only; stay in the family floors.

pois.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
pois.why: Free gardens on the old Edo Castle grounds, with huge stone walls and the keep's base.
pois.kid: Climb the old castle keep base for a view.

pois.name: Imperial Palace Plaza & Nijubashi
pois.why: The double bridge in front of the Emperor's palace.

pois.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
pois.why: Streets of seafood stalls, knife shops and tamagoyaki (sweet omelette) on sticks.
pois.kid: Try a slice of sweet omelette on a stick.
pois.tip: Best 8:00–11:00; many stalls close by early afternoon. Also some closures on Wednesdays.

pois.name: Hama-rikyu Gardens
pois.why: A tidal garden with a teahouse on a pond, framed by skyscrapers.

pois.name: Ginza
pois.why: Tokyo's smart shopping street; car-free on weekend afternoons.

pois.name: Shibuya Crossing
pois.why: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing: thousands cross at once when the lights change.
pois.kid: Cross it once, then watch it from above.

pois.name: Hachiko statue
pois.why: The statue of the loyal dog who waited for his owner every day for years.

pois.name: Shibuya Sky
pois.why: Open-air rooftop viewpoint over the crossing and the city.
pois.kid: Look straight down at the crossing from the edge.

pois.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
pois.why: A Shinto shrine in a forest of 100,000 trees, a calm world next to Harajuku.
pois.kid: Find the wall of sake barrels on the walk in.
pois.tip: Bow once at the big torii gate as you enter.

pois.name: Takeshita Street
pois.why: Harajuku's narrow street of colourful fashion and rainbow sweets.

pois.name: Yoyogi Park
pois.why: A big open park next to Meiji Jingu, lively on Sundays.

pois.name: Shinjuku Gyoen garden
pois.why: A huge garden mixing Japanese, French and English styles, with a greenhouse.

pois.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government observatory
pois.why: Free observation decks on the 45th floor of the city hall towers.
pois.kid: On a clear day, look for Mount Fuji to the west.

pois.name: Tokyo Tower
pois.why: The red-and-white 333 m tower from 1958, with a glass floor on the main deck.

pois.name: Zojo-ji Temple
pois.why: A big temple with Tokyo Tower rising behind it, and rows of small stone statues in red hats.

pois.name: teamLab Planets
pois.why: Walk barefoot through water and rooms of digital art.
pois.kid: Wade through the glowing koi pond.
pois.tip: Timed tickets; wear shorts or trousers you can roll up.

pois.name: Miraikan science museum
pois.why: Japan's future-science museum: robots, space and a giant globe.

pois.name: Odaiba Seaside Park
pois.why: A bayside beach walk with views of the Rainbow Bridge.

pois.name: Unicorn Gundam statue
pois.why: A life-size giant robot statue outside the DiverCity mall.

pois.name: Ghibli Museum
pois.why: The animation studio's own museum in Inokashira Park.
pois.tip: Tickets are released monthly and sell out fast: book as soon as they open.

pois.name: Shinjuku department store food hall
pois.why: A basement food hall (depachika) with bento boxes, sushi and sweets to take away.
pois.tip: Great for a picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen.

pois.name: Ginza department store food halls
pois.why: Basement food floors of the big Ginza stores: bento, sushi, cakes.

pois.name: Shibuya station food halls
pois.why: Station department stores with ready meals, plus ramen and conveyor-belt sushi nearby.

pois.name: Asakusa tempura and soba
pois.why: Old-style restaurants around Senso-ji serving tempura bowls and soba noodles.

pois.name: Ueno and Ameyoko lunch counters
pois.why: Cheap ramen, sushi and curry counters around Ueno station.

pois.name: Odaiba mall food courts
pois.why: Big food courts in the DiverCity and Aqua City malls.

dayTrips.name: Kamakura
dayTrips.from: JR Yokosuka line from Tokyo or Shinagawa
dayTrips.why: The Great Buddha, seaside temples and a surf beach.
dayTrips.tip: Go on a weekday; weekends are crowded.

dayTrips.name: Hakone
dayTrips.why: Hot springs, a ropeway over volcanic steam and a pirate ship on Lake Ashi, with views of Mount Fuji on clear days.
highlights: Black eggs boiled in volcanic springs
dayTrips.tip: The Hakone Free Pass covers trains, buses, ropeway and boat.

dayTrips.name: Nikko
dayTrips.why: Richly carved shrines in a cedar forest, plus waterfalls in the hills.
dayTrips.tip: A long day: take an early train.

dayTrips.name: Mount Takao
dayTrips.from: Keio line from Shinjuku to Takaosanguchi
dayTrips.why: An easy mountain hike with a cable car, a temple and Fuji views.
dayTrips.tip: Avoid weekends in autumn leaf season.

dayTrips.name: Yokohama
dayTrips.from: JR or Tokyu lines from Tokyo, Shibuya or Shinagawa
dayTrips.why: Japan's biggest Chinatown, a waterfront and the Cup Noodles Museum.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Get a Suica or PASMO card (or add one to your phone's wallet) and tap in and out. Children aged 6–11 pay half fare on a child card; under-6s ride free with an adult.

tips.title: Manners
tips.text: Speak quietly on trains, queue at the marked lines on platforms and don't eat while walking. Take shoes off where you see a step up and slippers.

tips.title: Money
tips.text: Cards work almost everywhere now, but carry some cash for small shops and temples. Tipping is not done.

tips.title: Food on the go
tips.text: Convenience stores (konbini) sell good onigiri, sandwiches and drinks around the clock. Department-store basements are the best picnic shops.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Tokyo is very safe. Police: 110. Fire and ambulance: 119. Earthquake info appears on phones automatically.

tips.title: Book ahead
tips.text: teamLab Planets, Shibuya Sky and the Ghibli Museum use timed tickets; Ghibli sells out weeks ahead.
